validity.researcher_notes: I could not find an independent source citing an exact length in km for HUT specifically (unlike the other three rows in this brief, where a regulator figure was available). CAG Report No. 21 of 2016 (Comptroller & Auditor General, Union Commercial Compliance Report No. 21 of 2016, 'Crude Oil Production Measurement and Reporting System' — cag.gov.in) quotes ONGC management describing 'MUT and HUT pipelines... over the 200 kms long pipeline' and, separately, 'the pipeline' as having 'large volume (200 KM pipeline)' when discussing residence time and emulsion break-up — but the wording is ambiguous as to which of the two lines (or whether both jointly) it describes, and elsewhere the report consistently treats MUT (30", from Mumbai High) as the larger/longer of the pair and HUT (24", from the closer Heera/satellite platform) as the shorter one (per the ONGC Uran Plant presentation on pdfcoffee.com cited in the FuelSource fill above). Geographically, Heera field sits roughly 110 km SW of Mumbai — closer to Uran than Mumbai High (~160 km NW) — so a priori HUT should be the SHORTER of the two trunks, consistent with the sheet's 80 km (vs MUT's 204 km) but inconsistent with the drawn route's 166 km, which is closer in magnitude to MUT's own drawn 146 km. RouteAccuracy on this row is already 'very low (straight line/schematic)': a schematic straight-line trace normally UNDERSHOOTS true pipeline length (it cuts corners a real seabed route would not), so a 2.08x OVERSHOOT is the wrong-direction artifact for that accuracy tier — it reads more like a mis-anchored endpoint or a route drawn via the wrong platform than a legitimately long line. I am not proposing a coordinate fix (standing rule against fabricating route geometry); recommending a geometry QA pass instead. Tier not assigned (no citable value either way) — this is reasoning from context, not a corroborated figure, so treat as UNRESOLVED-with-analysis rather than a confirmed finding.

MUT's oil share is captured on the oil/NGL side as GOIT P5191, giving the Uran system two linked GEM entries (P0944 gas + P5191 oil) for one physical pipeline. HUT (P0926) has no such GOIT counterpart that I could find, so its oil share appears untracked anywhere in GEM. This is a structural completeness question about GOIT coverage, not a value I can fill on the gas tab — flagging for a human/triage decision rather than proposing an edit.
